messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: GPU_SOFT_OOM rate spike in us-west2a (cuda_soft_oom_rate > 5% over 1m). Affected pool: g4-pool-3. PD: INC1234. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC1234

oncall-mia: Acked INC1234. I'm on it. @raj can you grab logs from nodes 12-16 and share quick triage?

raj: Pulling logs now. Seeing repeated 'cudaErrorMemoryAllocation' in /var/log/nvidia-driver.log on node-14. PIDs spiking: 2345, 6789. Tail: ```[12:34:56] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[12:34:57] evicting kvcache entry id=0x7f1a
[12:34:58] spawn retry for pid=2345```

sasha: Can you tell if it's kvcache eviction noise or app-side leak? Metrics show kvcache_evictions jumped at the same time as OOMs.

raj: kvcache_evictions ↑ 8x on that pool. Also noticed a batch-infer job from customer grammarly-inc accounting for ~30% of active sessions on g4-pool-3. High batch size + concurrency.

oncall-mia: If we can, temporarily reroute grammarly traffic to a lower-concurrency pool or fallback to cpu-async to stop noisy neighbor. Can someone flip routing?

sasha: I can change routing. Will set grammarly-inc max_concurrency=1 and add fallback to cpu-async. Doing a staged rollout.

deploy-bot: Starting rollout: routing-rule-update for customer=grammarly-inc -> max_concurrency=1, fallback=cpu-async. Canary 10% -> 100%.

sasha: Rolled to 30% then 100% within 45s. Verified grammarly traffic pegged to 1 concurrency.

raj: Memory pressure dropped on node-14 within ~2m. OOM events significantly reduced. Still see a couple of old-session errors but no new mass OOMs.

support-luis: Notifying support/AMs: impacted customers list prelim: grammarly-inc (high risk/degraded), startup-x (low). Drafting DM to grammarly AM now.

oncall-mia: Good. Keeping PD incident open for 30m of monitoring. Mitigation summary: routing throttle applied for grammarly + plan to tune kvcache eviction thresholds and per-customer quotas.

infra-bot: autopager: attempted auto-suppress for repeated alerts on this stream. autopager-suppress=true (10m) — manual ack retained.

raj: Next steps: open PR to adjust kvcache eviction aggressiveness and add hard cap on per-customer concurrent tokens. I'll create PR and tag @sasha for review.

sasha: Acknowledged. Will review the kvcache PR and coordinate a safe rollout window. Also propose adding a transient per-customer throttling rule in the router to prevent recurrence.

oncall-mia: Updated PD notes: mitigation applied. Customer impact: grammarly seeing ~10% latency bump while on fallback; no request errors after reroute. Keeping incident in watch state.

incident-bot: PagerDuty INC1234 status: acknowledged by oncall-mia. Incident remains open.

support-luis: Sent DM to grammarly AM — they acknowledged and appreciate the proactive reroute. Will escalate if they report data/sensitivity concerns (unlikely).

raj: Final log check: last observed OOM event timestamp 1738163500. No new OOMs in the last 8 minutes across g4-pool-3.

oncall-mia: Marking last_message_ts and continuing to watch for 30m. If stable, we'll close and file a short postmortem with follow-ups (kvcache tuning, routing quota). Thanks all for quick coord. :thumbsup:
